confirmed_claims: Rebuild reproducibility: build.sh on the current working tree reproduces all four manifest digests byte for byte (local repeat-build check, not a reproducible-build claim).
Full harness 2.3.0 passes 136/136 on darwin-arm64 and on linux-arm64 (K13) against my independent rebuild, so the stage's final conformance verdict reproduces.

K6d: an explicit SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT/SIGWINCH to the heimdall-proto pid reaches the child exactly once in every layout. Harness: sh -c and pipeline first/last. My probes add a wrapper script, a Makefile recipe (darwin), stdin<file and exclusive, under bash, zsh and dash, on both OSes.

K6a/K6c gated scope: under nohup the child inherits SIGHUP ignored, explicit SIGHUP is not forwarded, and heimdall-proto survives it, on both OSes and three shells. Inherited ignores of TSTP/TTIN/TTOU/CONT/INT/HUP also pass through.

K6e: Ctrl-Z/fg with a tty-reading child works under bash, zsh and dash on both OSes, for both exclusive and pipeline jobs, with no re-stop after fg (the Linux round-2 re-stop is fixed). Harness K6e passes on both OSes.

REPORT gap 5 (Q12) as described: after bg, a child that reads the tty is stopped by SIGTTIN, heimdall-proto mirrors the stop, and the shell lists the job as stopped (tty input), the same as the control. The child gets input after fg. Observed on both OSes under bash, zsh and dash.

REPORT gap 1 / K6b: in shared layouts a terminal ^C or resize reaches the child twice (pipeline 2, wrapper 2/2/2). Exclusive and stdin<file layouts deliver once. Documented in REPORT.md and allowed by K6b.

REPORT gap 2 refined: exclusive-mode hangup delivers the same number of SIGHUPs to the child as the same command without heimdall-proto (darwin bash 1/1, zsh 2/2, dash 1/1; Linux bash 2/2, zsh 2/2, dash 1/1). No duplicate added by heimdall-proto was observed.
K10: the TUI exits 143 on SIGTERM and 129 on SIGHUP and on both hangup variants (harness, both OSes). A TUI blocked waiting for input also exited 143 on SIGTERM in my probe.
K17: large-100 filter keystroke p95 is 17.7 ms (darwin) and 20.1 ms (linux), against the 100 ms bound.
K3a: Linux delivers real ECONNRESET in both positions and the harness K3a checks pass; darwin delivers EOF.
K15: 17 independent <=1 MiB shapes all finish within 0.06 s and 36 MiB peak RSS on both OSes, each accepted or rejected with SCHEMA_INVALID.
Round-2 terminfo defects are fixed: TERM traversal to /dev/zero, TERMINFO and TERMINFO_DIRS FIFOs, and the round-2 fuzz crash entry all draw within 30 ms and exit 0 on both OSes.

K16 and no stray writes: with TMUX, TERM_PROGRAM=tmux, TEA_TRACE, TEA_DEBUG, UV_DEBUG and GODEBUG set and logging stubs on PATH, no subcommand wrote any file or ran any helper, on both OSes. UV_DEBUG's file write in ultraviolet NewTerminalScreen is unreachable: Bubble Tea v2.0.10 constructs only NewTerminalRenderer/NewTerminalReader (code inspection plus runtime check).
Round-1 minors stay fixed: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES is blocked by the hardened runtime (the control gets injected), and the `.` PATH refusal (127) holds under GODEBUG=execerrdot=0/1.
Distribution: the darwin artifact runs under env -i with no Go on PATH and links only libSystem/libresolv. The linux-arm64 artifact is a static ELF and runs in python:3.13-alpine with no Go.
Licensing: all 18 linked modules are MIT or BSD-3-Clause, checked independently from the module cache license files. They match LICENSES.md.
REPORT.md line counts (2,382 non-test, 4,636 total) and the round-3b build table digests are accurate.
Builder tests reproduce: go test ./... exit 0, go vet (host and windows) 0, go mod verify 0, gofmt clean, govulncheck no findings on three binaries, selftest 75/75.
No full HEIMDALL_CANARY_ value in any review3 artifact. No leftover processes or containers.

summary: I could not refute the round-3b Go verdict. I rebuilt in /tmp, and all four digests match dist/manifest.json. Against that rebuild the full harness 2.3.0 passes 136/136 on darwin-arm64 and on linux-arm64 (exit 0 each). Independent pty probes covered bash, zsh and dash on both OSes, and layouts the harness does not test: wrapper script, Makefile recipe on darwin, nohup, stdin<file, Q12, explicit SIGTSTP, and hangup with a heartbeat child. They confirm K6d (an explicit signal reaches the child exactly once in every layout) and K6a/K6c gated ignores. They also confirm K6e and Q12 behave like the plain command, and terminal signals arrive once in exclusive mode and twice in shared mode (K6b, documented). Exclusive-mode hangup adds no SIGHUP over the control. The round-1 and round-2 defects I re-tested stay fixed: terminfo traversal/FIFO/panic, tmux exec, K15 (17 new shapes, at most 0.06 s and 36 MiB), DYLD injection, GODEBUG `.`-PATH. No stray writes or helper processes appeared under a hostile environment, and UV_DEBUG is unreachable. Distribution without a toolchain works and licensing matches LICENSES.md. go test, vet, mod verify, govulncheck and selftest 75/75 all exit 0. New findings, all minor and non-gating: (1) `run` drops a later duplicate environment entry, which REPORT.md does not disclose; (2) an explicit SIGTSTP to heimdall-proto in exclusive mode leaves the child running while the shell shows the job stopped, also undisclosed; (3) the stage summary misreads the harness's own double-kill probe (signal_duplicates 4/10 darwin, 0/10 linux) as heimdall-proto terminal-SIGINT duplicates; (4) the measured sources are uncommitted (+dirty), so a commit ID for the ADR is still needed. Windows/WSL were reviewed in code only. I hit and recorded several probe bugs of my own (pty drain, 0x0 window, a guessed image digest, pipe-masked exit codes); none is a prototype finding. No canary values in any artifact, and no leftover processes or containers.
